title: Kubernetes never runs your container. Here's why
caption: Pods explained in plain English. What runs in your Pods besides your app?

scenes.vo: Kubernetes never runs your container directly. It wraps it in a Pod, the smallest thing it can deploy. One or more containers, packed together.
scenes.heading: PODS

scenes.vo: Containers in the same Pod share one IP address and storage. So they talk over localhost, like roommates sharing one flat.
scenes.heading: INSIDE A POD

scenes.vo: But Pods are temporary. When one crashes, Kubernetes doesn't repair it. It throws it away and starts a new Pod, with a new IP.
scenes.heading: PODS ARE TEMPORARY

scenes.vo: That's why you rarely create Pods yourself. You write a Deployment, and say how many you want.
scenes.heading: THE TRICK?

scenes.vo: So, Pods: the smallest unit, a shared network, and fully disposable. Follow for more Kubernetes in plain English.
scenes.heading: PODS
